note: Second-generation oral PSMB5 (beta5 chymotrypsin-like) proteasome inhibitors (ixazomib, delanzomib, oprozomib) entered relapsed/refractory myeloma on human myeloma xenografts whose tumour proteasome inhibition and growth arrest translated, while the tolerability each programme claimed in animals missed thrombocytopenia, rash and gastrointestinal toxicity; bortezomib, carfilzomib and marizomib are the class context, not members.
label: Myeloma (PSMB5)

engagement.model: Delanzomib programme: human MM xenografts in immunodeficient mice with tumour-vs-normal-tissue proteasome PD
engagement.note: CEP-18770 gave sustained proteasome inhibition in xenograft tumours versus normal tissue; no patient PD yet (first in 2012, next entry).
engagement.quote: Intravenous and oral administration of CEP-18770 resulted in a more sustained pharmacodynamic inhibition of proteasome activity in tumors relative to normal tissues, complete tumor regression of MM xenografts and improved overall median survival in a systemic model of human MM.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Opener at first use; the patient proteasome-PD comparison is the track's 2012 entry (Gallerani 2013).
engagement.judgement: Delanzomib never filed an NDA, so no regulator record exists; the myeloma phase I/II paper (Vogl 2017, doi:10.1080/10428194.2016.1263842) gives no proteasome-activity readout in its abstract, but the first-in-human phase 1 (Gallerani 2013, epub 2012) does, scored as the track's 2012 entry. The opener is the model at first use, untested, not an empty cell.

engagement.model: Human MM.1S myeloma xenografts in CB-17 SCID mice; tumour 20S beta5 inhibition + unfolded-protein-response markers (ixazomib)
engagement.note: Ixazomib (MLN9708) gave greater tissue 20S proteasome inhibition and UPR-marker induction than bortezomib in xenografts; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: Tumour 20S inhibition is the model readout
engagement.quote: MLN9708 has a larger blood volume distribution at steady state, and analysis of 20S proteasome inhibition and markers of the unfolded protein response confirmed that MLN9708 has greater pharmacodynamic effects in tissues than bortezomib.
engagement.judgement: The FDA pharmacology review (NDA 208462) lists the MM.1S SCID PK/PD study (MLN9708-24699): tumour 20S beta5 inhibition Emax 71.7% (IV) and 60.6% (PO) with GADD34 and cleaved caspase-3 induction, so model_filed is true. Oprozomib's model (Chauhan 2010, doi:10.1182/blood-2010-04-276626) is the same MM.1S/SCID system from the same laboratory.

engagement.model: Human MM.1S myeloma xenografts in CB-17 SCID mice; tumour 20S beta5 inhibition + unfolded-protein-response markers (ixazomib)
engagement.note: In dosed patients, whole-blood 20S proteasome activity fell and ATF-3 rose in tumour biopsies: the mouse PD readouts moved in humans.
engagement.quote: Inhibition of whole-blood 20S proteasome activity and upregulation of ATF-3 in tumor biopsies demonstrated target engagement.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; no percentage inhibition is given to scale against the mouse tumour Emax (60-72%). Subjects were solid-tumour patients, not myeloma patients; engagement is not disease-restricted (healthy volunteers count), and the FDA clinical pharmacology review carries no PD data.
engagement.magnitude_basis: whole-blood 20S proteasome inhibition and tumour ATF-3 (UPR marker) present/absent; no numbers in the abstract to scale against the mouse tumour Emax
engagement.population: Advanced non-haematologic malignancies (NCT00830869); engagement read under the healthy-volunteer rule
engagement.reason: Mouse PD readouts moved in patients
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison: the mouse readout (tumour 20S beta5 inhibition, GADD34/caspase-3; FDA pharmacology review) against whole-blood 20S inhibition and tumour ATF-3 in the IV phase 1 (NCT00830869, results posted 2019-09-09). The two myeloma phase 1 abstracts (Richardson 2014 doi:10.1182/blood-2014-01-548826; Kumar 2014 doi:10.1182/blood-2014-01-548941) report PK only. Oprozomib adds a second class member: dose-dependent proteasome inhibition in red cells and PBMCs of solid-tumour patients (Infante 2016, doi:10.1007/s10637-016-0327-x), the readout Zhou 2009 used in rodents and dogs.

engagement.model: Delanzomib programme: human MM xenografts in immunodeficient mice with tumour-vs-normal-tissue proteasome PD
engagement.note: In the first-in-human phase 1, PBMC proteasome inhibition was dose related in MM patients (45.4% at the RD): the mouse proteasome-PD prediction held.
engagement.short: PBMC proteasome inhibition seen in patients
engagement.quote: Proteasome inhibition in peripheral blood mononuclear cells was dose related in MM patients; it was of 45.4±11.5% at the RD.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The patient readout is 20S proteasome activity in blood mononuclear cells, so the mouse claim of tumour-over-normal-tissue selectivity is not itself testable; Piva 2008 gives no blood-cell number to scale 45.4% against, so direction only. Mixed solid-tumour/MM phase 1; the PD datum is from the MM patients.
engagement.magnitude_basis: PBMC 20S proteasome inhibition in dosed MM patients (dose related; 45.4±11.5% at the RD) against the mouse proteasome-inhibition readout; no comparable blood-cell number in Piva 2008, so direction only
engagement.population: Advanced solid tumours and multiple myeloma (first-in-human phase 1); the PD datum is from the MM patients
engagement.reason: Mouse proteasome-PD readout moved in patients
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison (comparison_stated false): Piva 2008's mouse proteasome-inhibition readout (model_src) against dose-related PBMC proteasome inhibition in the MM patients of the first-in-human phase 1 (Gallerani 2013, epub 2012-10-08, so year 2012 under dating rule 6). Blood mononuclear cells stand in for the tissue readout, as on the ixazomib track; the mouse tumour-over-normal selectivity claim is not testable in patients, so the match is in direction only. Prospective (the phase 1 followed the model), so same, not retro. Placed at the end of the cell so the check file's positional verdict indexes for the two ixazomib entries stay valid; figure.py sorts by year. Registry: the EOS phase 1 NCT00572637 (started 2007-11) has no results posted and the abstract names no NCT, so registry_date is null.

dose.model: Delanzomib programme: human MM xenografts in immunodeficient mice with tumour-vs-normal-tissue proteasome PD
dose.note: Mouse PD set no human exposure target; the phase I/II escalated to a toxicity-defined MTD. No comparison yet.
dose.short: Mouse PD set no human target
dose.quote: Intravenous and oral administration of CEP-18770 resulted in a more sustained pharmacodynamic inhibition of proteasome activity in tumors relative to normal tissues, complete tumor regression of MM xenografts and improved overall median survival in a systemic model of human MM.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; mouse doses and exposures are not in the abstract.
dose.judgement: Opens the delanzomib track at first use.

dose.model: Human MM.1S myeloma xenografts in CB-17 SCID mice; tumour 20S beta5 inhibition + unfolded-protein-response markers (ixazomib)
dose.note: Oral gavage reached tumour-active exposure in xenografts (99% TGI at 6 mg/kg twice weekly); no human exposure comparison yet.
dose.quote: Moreover, antitumor activity was shown via multiple dosing routes, including oral gavage.
dose.judgement: The FDA pharmacology review gives the mouse numbers: 6 mg/kg PO single dose, plasma AUC0-24 1,680 h*ng/mL, tumour AUC0-24 16,100 h*ng/mL; 6-10 mg/kg PO twice weekly gave 99-100% tumour growth inhibition (studies MLN9708-24699 and -24176).

dose.model: Human MM.1S myeloma xenografts in CB-17 SCID mice; tumour 20S beta5 inhibition + unfolded-protein-response markers (ixazomib)
dose.note: Oral 4 mg weekly gave a per-dose plasma AUC within 2x of the mouse's tumour-active dose, was tolerated, and carried the PFS benefit.
dose.quote: Following multiple-dose administration, plasma exposure of ixazomib generally increased dose proportionally over a dose range of 0.48 to 3.95 mg/m2 (1.4 to 8.9 mg actual administered).
dose.confidence_note: The mouse figure is a single-dose AUC0-24 at 6 mg/kg (nonclinical t1/2 30-72 h, so it under-reads total exposure); per week the mouse twice-weekly regimen delivered 2-4x the patient's once-weekly exposure. The once-weekly regimen itself was chosen on human half-life and phase 1 tolerability, not on the mouse.
dose.magnitude_basis: per-dose plasma AUC: mouse 6 mg/kg PO (99% TGI regimen) AUC0-24 1,680 vs patient 4 mg AUC0-last 1,160 h*ng/mL (FDA ClinPharm review Table 4), ratio 1.4
dose.reason: Oral exposure reached; PFS benefit followed
dose.judgement: Paired comparison of the FDA pharmacology review (mouse PK/PD) with the clinical pharmacology review (patient PK). Enough: TOURMALINE-MM1 (NCT01564537, results posted 2016-01-27) met PFS at 4 mg weekly. margin_stated is true under decision 16: the review states a dog NOAEL with an approximately 2-fold separation from extensive neuronal pathology (neuronal effects at 4 mg/m2, AUC0-168 1,940 h*ng/mL); patients at 4 mg (about 2.2 mg/m2; day-1 AUC0-168 846, roughly 2-fold accumulation at steady state) were dosed to target with peripheral neuropathy mostly grade 1-2 (grade 3 in 2%, same as placebo), so the margin held. Regimen: the sponsor picked once weekly over twice weekly on phase 1 response (30% vs 15%) and tolerability (ClinPharm review, Dose Selection); the FDA pharmacology review lists an IV once- vs twice-weekly MM.1S study (MLN9708-24177) but does not excerpt its result, so the mouse is not credited with the regimen. Oprozomib is not scored here: it reached dose-dependent proteasome inhibition and responses (Infante 2016; Ghobrial 2019), and its halt was tolerability and formulation PK, scored in safety.

dose.model: Delanzomib programme: human MM xenografts in immunodeficient mice with tumour-vs-normal-tissue proteasome PD
dose.note: Delanzomib was dosed to its MTD (2.1 mg/m2 weekly) and failed on response; the sponsor abandoned it. Dose failure derived from efficacy.
dose.quote: At the MTD, 26 patients (55%) had stable disease and four (9%) had a partial response (PR).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The MTD was capped by rash and thrombocytopenia DLTs at 2.4 mg/m2 and neither abstract gives exposures, so whether the mouse-effective exposure was ever reached is unknown; if it was not, this entry would be untested (no stated margin for those harms), not contra. Scored on the authors' own attribution of the discontinuation to efficacy. NCT01023880 has no results posted.
dose.reason: Dose reached; drug failed on efficacy
dose.judgement: Table row 'reached, failed, abandoned': dose contra derived_from efficacy so the one failure is counted once. The thrombocytopenia and rash that set the MTD were not predicted by the model and are scored in safety, not here (decision 16).

dose.model: Ixazomib population-PK model (NONMEM, 226 phase 1 patients) simulating exposure after fixed 4 mg versus BSA-based 2.23 mg/m2 dosing
dose.note: PopPK of 226 phase 1 patients predicted fixed 4 mg gives the same AUC as 2.23 mg/m2 across body sizes; the phase 3 run at 4 mg had not read out.
dose.quote: there was no relationship between BSA and ixazomib clearance (the parameter that dictates total systemic exposure following fixed dosing)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The sponsor ran the analysis during phase 2 (FDA ClinPharmR: 'During Phase 2 evaluations, the sponsor's population PK analysis determined that body size does not significantly influence'); the 2015 paper is the earliest public record, so the track opens there.
dose.population: Phase 1 MM, lymphoma and solid-tumour patients on BSA-based ixazomib
dose.judgement: An in-silico dose-selection model under the brief's 'in-silico / QSP models used to choose doses'. Its stated target is exposure equivalence of fixed 4 mg to the 2.23 mg/m2 RP2D, which the phase 3 then tested.

dose.model: Ixazomib population-PK model (NONMEM, 226 phase 1 patients) simulating exposure after fixed 4 mg versus BSA-based 2.23 mg/m2 dosing
dose.note: FDA's popPK review of phase 3 data found body size does not move clearance; 4 mg fixed reached the predicted exposure and TOURMALINE-MM1 met its PFS primary.
dose.short: Fixed 4 mg reached target and worked
dose.quote: however it was not found to influence ixazomib central clearance or volume of distribution. This supports sponsor’s fixed dosing approach.
dose.confidence_note: Quote from the OCRed review text in the source bundle (sources/208462). Gupta 2017 (doi 10.1007/s40262-017-0526-4; 755 patients including TOURMALINE-MM1) confirms BSA 1.2-2.7 m2 is not a clearance covariate.
dose.magnitude_basis: simulated AUC after fixed 4 mg (Gupta 2015) vs popPK-estimated phase 3 exposure, BSA 1.2-2.7 m2 without a clearance effect
dose.population: Relapsed/refractory MM, TOURMALINE-MM1 (ixazomib 4 mg fixed, days 1, 8, 15)
dose.reason: Fixed 4 mg reached target and worked
dose.judgement: Dose rule 'reached, drug worked': the model's exposure target (AUC of the 2.23 mg/m2 RP2D) was reached at 4 mg fixed in the phase 3 population and the primary PFS was met (FDA SumR, on the mm1s-scid-xenograft efficacy track). comparison_stated true: the regulator's own popPK review puts model and patient data side by side. Dated 2015 with the review (approval 2015-11-20), before the registry posting (2016-01-27). No tolerability margin is stated by this model, so margin_stated false.

efficacy.model: Delanzomib programme: human MM xenografts in immunodeficient mice with tumour-vs-normal-tissue proteasome PD
efficacy.note: CEP-18770 produced complete regression of MM xenografts and longer survival in a systemic MM model; no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: Intravenous and oral administration of CEP-18770 resulted in a more sustained pharmacodynamic inhibition of proteasome activity in tumors relative to normal tissues, complete tumor regression of MM xenografts and improved overall median survival in a systemic model of human MM.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from the ixazomib MM.1S/SCID system under this run's track rule: a different sponsor's xenograft panel (cell lines not named in the abstract) making a different prediction, parity with bortezomib plus marrow sparing.

efficacy.model: Human MM.1S myeloma xenografts in CB-17 SCID mice; tumour 20S beta5 inhibition + unfolded-protein-response markers (ixazomib)
efficacy.note: Ixazomib shrank haematologic and solid xenografts, with greater PD response tracking greater antitumour activity; no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: MLN9708 showed activity in both solid tumor and hematologic preclinical xenograft models, and we found a correlation between greater pharmacodynamic responses and improved antitumor activity.
efficacy.judgement: Myeloma-specific MM.1S/SCID data followed in Chauhan 2011 (doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-0476) and in the FDA pharmacology review (99-100% TGI at 6-10 mg/kg PO twice weekly).

efficacy.model: Human MM.1S myeloma xenografts in CB-17 SCID mice; tumour 20S beta5 inhibition + unfolded-protein-response markers (ixazomib)
efficacy.note: TOURMALINE-MM1 met its primary endpoint: PFS 20.6 vs 14.7 months, HR 0.74, adding ixazomib to lenalidomide-dexamethasone.
efficacy.quote: Based on the 1st interim analysis (IA) of PFS, the estimated hazard ratio (HR) for PFS was 0.74 (95% confidence interval: 0.59 – 0.94, p-value = 0.01) for the Ixazomib arm versus Placebo arm
efficacy.confidence_note: The FDA review notes the updated final PFS analysis (HR 0.82, p=0.0548) did not reach significance and that IRC and investigator PFS were discordant; approval rested on the pre-specified interim. Status follows the pre-specified primary analysis.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse tumour growth inhibition (99% at 6 mg/kg) is not commensurable with a PFS hazard ratio (0.74); direction only

patient_trials.quote: median progression-free survival, 20.6 months vs. 14.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death in the ixazomib group, 0.74; P=0.01
In phase II, ORRs in 95 response-eligible multiple myeloma patients were 41.0%, 28.1%, and 25.0% in the 2/7, 240/300-mg/day; 5/14, 150/180-mg/day; and 5/14, 240-mg/day cohorts, respectively.

efficacy.judgement: Dated 2015 because the FDA review package (approval 2015-11-20) made the comparison public before the registry posting (2016-01-27) and the NEJM paper (Moreau 2016, in patient_trials). The xenograft is a single-agent model; the trial was an add-on to lenalidomide-dexamethasone, and single-agent ixazomib in phase 1 gave 15-18% ORR (Richardson 2014; Kumar 2014), so magnitude is direction only. Oprozomib, the other member on this model system (Chauhan 2010, MM.1S/SCID), also responded in the same direction (ORR 41% on the 2/7 schedule, Ghobrial 2019) and is listed in patient_trials rather than as a separate entry. OS, a key secondary, is not an outcome trial of a surrogate, so outcome_tested stays null.

efficacy.model: Delanzomib programme: human MM xenografts in immunodeficient mice with tumour-vs-normal-tissue proteasome PD
efficacy.note: At the MTD delanzomib gave 9% partial responses and 2.5-month TTP against complete regressions in mice; development stopped for efficacy.
efficacy.quote: Based upon the efficacy results, development of delanzomib for myeloma was discontinued.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The MTD was set by rash and thrombocytopenia DLTs at 2.4 mg/m2, so the mouse-effective exposure may never have been reached; if a full-text exposure comparison showed that, this would be untested rather than contra. NCT01023880 (phase I/II, primary endpoint ORR) has no results posted.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ORR 9% (4/47 PR) at the MTD, median TTP 2.5 months, versus complete tumour regression in mice

patient_trials.quote: At the MTD, 26 patients (55%) had stable disease and four (9%) had a partial response (PR).

efficacy.judgement: The paper itself attributes discontinuation to efficacy (source_calls_it: miss). Piva 2008 predicted a profile 'competitive with bortezomib'; single-agent bortezomib in comparable relapsed/refractory patients gave roughly 27-38% ORR, so 9% is below the class bar, but no model effect size and class threshold are quotable from the abstract, so this is contra rather than neg. This failure stays on the delanzomib track and does not touch the ixazomib MM.1S/SCID track.

efficacy.model: Patient-derived primary CD138+ myeloma cells ex vivo, including cells from bortezomib-treated or bortezomib-resistant patients (Piva 2008; Chauhan 2010, 2011)
efficacy.note: CEP-18770 killed CD138+ explants from untreated and bortezomib-treated patients; ONX 0912 (2010) and MLN2238 (2011) later killed bortezomib-resistant patient cells. No patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: Bortezomib-treated patients' cells respond ex vivo
efficacy.quote: CEP-18770 induces apoptotic cell death in multiple myeloma (MM) cell lines and in primary purified CD138-positive explant cultures from untreated and bortezomib-treated MM patients.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The explant result is pooled across patients, not a per-patient prediction; the same system carried oprozomib (Chauhan 2010, doi 10.1182/blood-2010-04-276626) and ixazomib (Chauhan 2011, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-0476).
efficacy.population: CD138+ cells from untreated and bortezomib-treated MM patients
efficacy.judgement: Opened at first use (Piva 2008, epub 2007-12-05). Patient-level track: the system's claim is that cells from bortezomib-exposed or bortezomib-resistant patients still die on a member drug, i.e. which patients respond, not whether the class works. Separate from the cell-line xenograft tracks: different material, different prediction.

efficacy.model: Patient-derived primary CD138+ myeloma cells ex vivo, including cells from bortezomib-treated or bortezomib-resistant patients (Piva 2008; Chauhan 2010, 2011)
efficacy.note: Single-agent ixazomib gave PRs in the bortezomib-relapsed (3/10) and relapsed-refractory (2/11) expansion cohorts, as bortezomib-resistant patient cells ex vivo predicted.
efficacy.short: Responses after bortezomib, as ex vivo predicted
efficacy.quote: Responses were seen across the expansion cohorts, including 2, 3, 1, and 2 PRs in the relapsed and refractory, bortezomib-relapsed, PI-naive, and prior carfilzomib cohorts, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via the publisher page. Cohorts of 10-11 patients; no bortezomib-refractory cohort is reported, response was a secondary endpoint of a safety-primary phase 1, and the ex-vivo data were pooled across patients, so the match is direction only.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex vivo apoptosis in bortezomib-resistant patient cells (Chauhan 2011) vs PR rate in the bortezomib-relapsed cohort (3/10); no common scale
efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory MM, weekly single-agent ixazomib expansion cohorts by prior bortezomib/carfilzomib exposure (NCT00963820)

patient_trials.quote: Among 55 response-evaluable patients, 15% achieved partial response or better (76% stable disease or better).
In phase II, ORRs in 95 response-eligible multiple myeloma patients were 41.0%, 28.1%, and 25.0% in the 2/7, 240/300-mg/day; 5/14, 150/180-mg/day; and 5/14, 240-mg/day cohorts, respectively.
At the MTD, 26 patients (55%) had stable disease and four (9%) had a partial response (PR).

efficacy.reason: Responses after bortezomib, as ex vivo predicted
efficacy.judgement: Scored same rather than untested because Kumar 2014 reports responses by prior-bortezomib cohort, which is the patient-level question the ex-vivo system asked (Chauhan 2011: MLN2238 kills MM cells resistant to bortezomib therapy). Paired comparison: the trial paper only cites the model work. The FDA pharmacology review reproduces Chauhan 2011's ex-vivo cytotoxicity figure, so model_filed is true for ixazomib. endpoint_role null: ORR was a secondary endpoint of a safety-primary phase 1. Richardson 2014 (88% prior bortezomib, 15% ORR), oprozomib (Ghobrial 2019) and delanzomib (Vogl 2017, 9% PR) are same-direction and change no status; none reports a bortezomib-refractory subgroup. No source compares a patient's own ex-vivo result with that patient's clinical response to a member drug.

efficacy.model: Berenson-lab SCID-hu LAGκ-1A (bortezomib-sensitive) and LAGκ-1B (bortezomib-resistant) patient-derived myeloma xenografts, dosed with delanzomib
efficacy.note: Oral single-agent CEP-18770 gave marked anti-MM effects in patient-derived LAGκ xenografts and, with bortezomib, delayed bortezomib-resistant tumours; no patient result yet.
efficacy.short: Oral single-agent activity in patient-derived xenografts
efficacy.quote: Single agent CEP-18770 PO also showed marked anti-MM effects in these xenograft models.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). The LAGκ-1A/-1B identity of the bortezomib-sensitive and bortezomib-resistant tumours comes from the Berenson-lab companion reports (ASH 2008 abstract 'Oral dosing of ... CEP-18770 ... in SCID-hu models'; Berenson 2012 Leuk Res, doi 10.1016/j.leukres.2012.07.018), not from this abstract.
efficacy.judgement: A separate track from delanzomib-mm-xenograft (Piva 2008, Cephalon cell-line xenografts): a different laboratory's patient-derived SCID-hu system with its own prediction (single-agent oral activity, retained activity against bortezomib-resistant disease in combination). Opened at the BJH epub (2009-12-01); the ASH 2008 abstract is earlier but was not verified beyond a search snippet.

efficacy.model: Berenson-lab SCID-hu LAGκ-1A (bortezomib-sensitive) and LAGκ-1B (bortezomib-resistant) patient-derived myeloma xenografts, dosed with delanzomib
efficacy.note: Single-agent delanzomib at the MTD gave 9% PR and development stopped, against marked single-agent activity in the LAGκ patient-derived xenografts.
efficacy.quote: At the MTD, 26 patients (55%) had stable disease and four (9%) had a partial response (PR).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT01023880 (ORR primary) terminated with no posted results. The combination prediction (delanzomib + dexamethasone/lenalidomide, Berenson 2012) reached NCT01348919: ORR 40% at the 1.8 mg/m2 MTD in a 5-patient cohort of 11 enrolled, results posted 2023-06-28, which changes no status.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft tumour growth inhibition vs single-agent PR rate (9%); not commensurable
efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory MM, single-agent delanzomib phase I/II (NCT01023880)

patient_trials.quote: Overall Response Rate (ORR) in Participants Treated at the (Maximum Tolerated Dose) MTD, as Assessed Using International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) Criteria: 40 percentage of participants (95% CI 5.27 to 85.34)

efficacy.judgement: Same patient datum as the delanzomib-mm-xenograft contra, scored on its own track because the systems differ. Contra, not neg: the abstract gives no model effect size below a class bar. Dated 2017 (epub 2017-01-31); the trial posted no registry results. The LAGκ-1B bortezomib-resistant arm was only tested in combination with bortezomib in mice and never in patients, so the patient-level half of the prediction stays untested. The NCT01348919 patient_trials quote is the registry outcome-measure title and value, not prose.

safety.model: Delanzomib programme: human MM xenografts in immunodeficient mice plus normal human bone-marrow progenitor and stromal cultures
safety.note: The model's stated prediction was marrow sparing: CEP-18770 spared normal epithelial cells, bone-marrow progenitors and stroma. No patient data yet.
safety.quote: Importantly, CEP-18770 exhibits a favorable cytotoxicity profile toward normal human epithelial cells, bone marrow progenitors, and bone marrow-derived stromal cells.
safety.judgement: model_kind is animal for the programme as a whole; the marrow-sparing claim itself came from ex vivo human bone-marrow progenitor cultures in the same paper.

safety.model: Ixazomib GLP toxicology: 6-month rat and 9-month dog oral repeat-dose studies
safety.note: Rat and dog studies flagged gastrointestinal, lymphoid/hepatic and (dog) dorsal-root-ganglion neuronal toxicity before patients were dosed.
safety.quote: Nonclinical findings in the rat and dog show that ixazomib targets the gastrointestinal tract, hematopoietic and lymphatic systems, nervous system (dog only).
safety.confidence_note: Proxy date: IND-enabling rat and dog studies preceded the March 2009 phase 1 start (NCT00830869); the 2015 FDA review is the public record. Its hematology tables are images in the OCR text, so platelet findings cannot be read; the review text names only white-cell changes.
safety.judgement: A different system from the xenograft tracks (GLP toxicology, not an efficacy model) with a different prediction (target organs and a dog NOAEL), so it is its own track under this run's rule.

safety.model: Oprozomib (PR-047/ONX 0912) rodent and dog repeat oral dosing plus xenografts
safety.note: Rodents and dogs tolerated repeated oral PR-047 at doses giving >80% proteasome inhibition in most tissues. No patient data yet.
safety.quote: It was well tolerated with repeated oral administration at doses resulting in >80% proteasome inhibition in most tissues and elicited an antitumor response equivalent to intravenously administered carfilzomib in multiple human tumor xenograft and mouse syngeneic models.
safety.judgement: Dogs can vomit and rodents show diarrhoea and weight loss, so gastrointestinal harm is one this system could have shown. Oprozomib never filed an NDA; its GLP toxicology is not public, so the published tolerability claim is the model statement scored.

safety.model: Ixazomib GLP toxicology: 6-month rat and 9-month dog oral repeat-dose studies
safety.note: GI toxicity, hepatotoxicity and peripheral neuropathy appeared in patients as rat/dog predicted; thrombocytopenia and rash were not in the animal findings.
safety.short: GI, neuropathy predicted; rash, platelets missed
safety.quote: The risks demonstrated, mainly gastrointestinal disorders, rash, thrombocytopenia and cutaneous reactions are acceptable and do not outweigh the benefit.
safety.confidence_note: Thrombocytopenia and rash are scored as unpredicted because the pharmacology review text lists no platelet or skin finding in rat or dog; its hematology tables are images and could not be read, so a platelet signal may exist in the submission.
safety.magnitude_basis: predicted target organs present or absent in TOURMALINE-MM1 warnings; no incidence can be scaled from histopathology
safety.reason: GI, neuropathy predicted; rash, platelets missed
safety.judgement: Paired comparison of the FDA pharmacology review (rat: GI and liver injury, lymphoid depletion; dog: dorsal-root-ganglion and peripheral-nerve degeneration, 2-fold NOAEL separation) with the summary review and TOURMALINE-MM1 (Moreau 2016, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1516282): label warnings for GI toxicity, hepatotoxicity and peripheral neuropathy (27% vs 22%, grade 3 2% each arm) match; grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia (12%/7% vs 5%/4%) and rash (36% vs 23%) were not predicted, though rats and dogs can show both. Partial match, so same with source_calls_it partial; the dog margin that held is scored in dose (decision 16), not twice here. The MM.1S xenograft papers also called ixazomib 'well tolerated' (Chauhan 2011) and are not scored separately: the rat/dog package is the system the sponsor relied on for harm.

safety.model: Delanzomib programme: human MM xenografts in immunodeficient mice plus normal human bone-marrow progenitor and stromal cultures
safety.note: Marrow sparing did not hold: rash and thrombocytopenia were the DLTs, and grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia hit 53% of patients at the MTD.
safety.quote: Dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) at 2.4 mg/m2 were rash and thrombocytopenia.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; NCT01023880 has no results posted. Delanzomib's own GLP toxicology was never made public (no NDA), so only the published model claim can be scored.
safety.magnitude_basis: marrow sparing predicted versus grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia in 53% and neutropenia in 23% at the MTD
safety.judgement: A stated prediction that failed, not a silence: the model claimed a favourable profile toward bone-marrow progenitors, and thrombocytopenia set the MTD. Counted here rather than in dose because the model did not predict the harm at all (decision 16). Rash was likewise unpredicted; the model was silent on skin and the harm is one mice could have shown.

safety.model: Oprozomib (PR-047/ONX 0912) rodent and dog repeat oral dosing plus xenografts
safety.note: Gastrointestinal AEs were the commonest grade 3+ events, three AE-related deaths forced step-up dosing, and the programme was halted for safety and formulation PK.
safety.short: Tolerated in dogs; GI toxicity ended programme
safety.quote: The most common grade ≥3 adverse events (AE) in phase Ib included gastrointestinal and hematologic AEs.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; NCT01416428 has no results posted. The halt is recorded by the registry (tier 3) rather than a paper.
safety.magnitude_basis: tolerated at >80% proteasome inhibition predicted versus dose-limiting gastrointestinal toxicity and AE-related deaths in myeloma patients
safety.reason: Tolerated in dogs; GI toxicity ended programme
safety.judgement: The GI signal was first seen in solid-tumour patients (Infante 2016, doi:10.1007/s10637-016-0327-x: nausea 91%, vomiting 86%, diarrhoea 61%, 'clinically relevant gastrointestinal toxicities occurred frequently with this oprozomib formulation'); the entry is dated to the myeloma paper rather than importing from another indication. The halt: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01881789 (results posted 2021-03-03) states 'A program evaluation identified that the safety profile and pharmacokinetic (PK) characteristics of the formulation used in all oprozomib studies required further optimization and thus enrollment in OPZ003 was halted during dose-escalation.' Hari 2019 (doi:10.1038/s41408-019-0232-6) is the NDMM paper; its abstract was not retrievable here.
